events.title: Supreme Court grants certiorari in Busby v. Mississippi
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion of petitioner Jeffrey D. Busby for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and the petition for a writ of certiorari. The judgment was vacated, and the case was remanded to the Supreme Court of Mississippi for further consideration in light of the position asserted by Mississippi in its brief filed on May 14, 2026. This allows the case to be re-examined by the state court with the new considerations in mind.
events.why_relevant: This decision highlights the Supreme Court's oversight function in ensuring that state court decisions are revisited when new legal arguments are presented.

events.title: Supreme Court grants certiorari in Grayson v. United States
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Grayson v. United States, vacated the judgment, and remanded the case to the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. This decision was made for further consideration in light of the position asserted by the Solicitor General in his brief for the United States filed on May 12, 2026. The case will be re-evaluated by the appellate court based on the new arguments presented by the Solicitor General.
events.why_relevant: This action reflects the Supreme Court's function in ensuring that appellate court decisions are reconsidered in light of new legal positions from the federal government.

events.title: Supreme Court grants certiorari in Newberry v. Texas
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Newberry v. Texas, vacated the judgment, and remanded the case to the Court of Criminal Appeals of Texas. This decision was made for further consideration in light of the position asserted by Texas in its brief filed on April 15, 2026. The case will be re-evaluated by the lower court based on the new arguments presented by Texas.
events.why_relevant: This action demonstrates the Supreme Court's role in ensuring that lower court decisions are reconsidered in light of new legal arguments or positions.

events.title: Supreme Court reverses Second Circuit in McCarthy v. Hernandez
events.summary: The Supreme Court reversed the Second Circuit's decision in McCarthy v. Hernandez, which had granted habeas relief based on the application of Missouri v. Seibert. The Supreme Court found that the Second Circuit exceeded its authority under AEDPA by misapplying federal law regarding jury instructions on confession attenuation. The case was remanded for further proceedings consistent with the Supreme Court's opinion.
events.why_relevant: This decision underscores the Supreme Court's role in correcting lower court misapplications of federal law, particularly in the context of habeas corpus and jury instructions.

events.title: Supreme Court denies stay of execution and certiorari in Spencer v. Florida
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States denied both the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Dusty R. Spencer v. Florida. The application was initially presented to Justice Thomas, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of the death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of a stay of execution and certiorari affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.

events.title: Supreme Court stays mandate in Catherine Herridge v. Yanping Chen
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States issued an order staying the mandate of the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in the case of Catherine Herridge v. Yanping Chen, case No. 24-5050. The stay is pending further order from the Chief Justice or the Court. Additionally, a response to the application is required to be filed by July 1, 2026, by 12 p.m. (EDT).
events.why_relevant: The stay affects the enforcement of the appellate court's decision, pending further review by the Supreme Court.
